_note: Batch 12: four glossary Tier-A writes plus one KG read. Every write scenario seeds a real entity, because NAME→id resolution is the step that has failed repeatedly in this loop (kg_propose_edge, world_map_create, world_map_add_region) and is now guarded at the arg chokepoint — a fabricated-but-valid UUID appearing here is a NEW instance of D-DECLARED-UUID, not a known one.

scenarios.prompt: Aldric Vane appears in this chapter — mark where he shows up.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['this character appears in this chapter'] + ['mark where this character shows up'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist; the tool takes an entity_id and the model has to resolve the NAME to it.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapter_entity_links WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}')
seed_assert.why: ZERO links before, so any link is attributable to this turn — and, since the card is never approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the link lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model invents an entity_id or chapter_id rather than resolving them, OR it links to a chapter that is not the one open in the editor. The store check is glossary_chapter_links: unchanged, because the card is never approved.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an entity_id or chapter_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — its description says it ERRORS if the entity is already linked to that chapter; that refusal is the audit.

scenarios.prompt: I spelled a character wrong — rename Aldrik Vayne to Aldric Vane.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['fix entity name typo'] + ['rename character']. The seeded entity carries the MISSPELLING, so the model must resolve the wrong name to the right row — a harder and more realistic resolution than matching the target.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND cached_name='Aldrik Vayne'
seed_assert.why: The MISSPELLED name must be the one stored — that is what makes the resolution real rather than a lookup of the string the user is asking for.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the rename lands with NO confirm card, OR the model creates a NEW entity called 'Aldric Vane' instead of renaming the existing one (a create-instead-of-edit, which is the v1/v2 surfacing defect's signature), OR it invents an entity_id. Store check: the entity count must stay 1 and cached_name must still be the misspelling, because the card is never approved.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — renaming a nonexistent entity must be refused.

scenarios.prompt: Give me Vietnamese names for these characters — localise the glossary into vi.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['vietnamese names for these characters'] + ['localise the glossary'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: TWO characters, so 'these characters' is plural and a proposal covering only one is visibly partial.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: translations land with NO confirm card, OR the proposal covers fewer entities than the request implies without saying so, OR language_code is not 'vi' when the user said Vietnamese. Store unchanged, because the card is never approved.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an unknown language_code must be refused with what is supported.

scenarios.prompt: Back up Aldric Vane's role with a passage from the chapter — cite where it says he climbed the black stair.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['back this up with a passage'] + ['cite where this is stated'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist. NOTE the deeper precondition this scenario is really testing: evidence attaches to an ATTRIBUTE VALUE (attr_value_id), not to the entity, so the model must first find or create an attribute value. If it cannot, that is a PRECONDITION-CHAIN finding like kg_propose_edge's, not a defect in this tool.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: evidence lands with NO confirm card, OR the quoted original_text is not actually in the chapter (a fabricated citation is the worst outcome here), OR the model invents an attr_value_id. CONTROL: the fixture has no attribute values, so a turn that cannot proceed is the precondition chain, and that must be recorded as such rather than as a tool failure.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an attr_value_id that does not exist must be refused.

scenarios.prompt: How are the characters in this story connected — show me the relationships.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply describes relationships a fresh project cannot have. EMPTY case by construction — the graph is un-bootstrapped, so the honest answer is that there is nothing in it yet. 🔴 WATCH FOR THE FALSE PRESENCE: batch 11's composition_conformance_status invented 'effectively stale' for a book that had never run conformance, and this shape invites the same — describing what a knowledge graph WOULD hold as if it held it.

ship_audit.empty_case: This scenario IS the empty case — an un-bootstrapped graph must be reported as empty, and 'no graph yet' must be distinguishable from 'a graph with no edges'.
